description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” of various multilingual BERT models on four morphosyntactic features — case, gender, number, and tense — as evaluated in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The horizontal axis categorizes the linguistic features (case, gender, number, tense), while the vertical axis represents the effect magnitude, ranging from 0 to 20 with tick marks at intervals of 5. Each feature group contains six bars corresponding to different model variants: XLM-L₂ (light blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (pink), and XLM-B₂ (red), as indicated in the legend. Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals. For “case,” the mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ models show the highest effect (around 12), followed by XLM-L₂ and XLM-R₂ (around 5–6), while mBERT-R₂ is slightly lower (~3). In “gender,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ again show the strongest effect (~4), with other models hovering near 1–2. For “number,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ again lead (~3), while others are near 1. In “tense,” all models show minimal effect (near 0–1), with XLM-B₂ slightly higher. The chart suggests that B₂ variants (particularly mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂) consistently outperform others across most features, with case showing the largest overall effect and tense the smallest.
